description.narrative: The youth employment portfolio in Mozambique is a collaborative effort by UNDP, government institutions (coordinated by the Ministry of Youth and Sports), development partners, civil society, academia, the private sector, and community-based organizations. Its goal is to strengthen partnerships and networks, address labor market needs, and implement targeted strategies such as the formalization and registration of the informal sector, professional training, the creation of cooperatives, private sector engagement, tax reduction advocacy, MSME financing, and the integration of youth into areas such as digitalization, new technologies, and artificial intelligence. Additionally, the portfolio ensures the empowerment of vulnerable youth, social reintegration for young people in conflict with the law, and the promotion of gender inclusivity.As we embark on this journey of portfolio development, it is essential to acknowledge that we are all navigating new terrain. In the context of youth employment, it is crucial for UNDP and all partners involved not only to review their work on youth employability but, more importantly, to gain a deeper understanding of the context, the various interventions, and the stakeholders involved, as well as how to position themselves to contribute to meaningful impact.The weak absorption capacity of young people in the labor market remains a significant challenge in Mozambique, with young women facing even greater obstacles due to discrimination, cultural barriers, and limited access to education and training opportunities.By promoting gender-inclusive and sustainable approaches, Mozambique can create the conditions for a fairer society where young people have the skills and resources needed to compete in the labor market—ultimately driving economic growth, upholding human rights, and ensuring equal access to employment opportunities.
